newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon delays local elections again.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon delays local elections again.

text.p: The Lebanese parliament has delayed for a second time nationwide local elections originally scheduled for June, voting to postpone them until April 1999.

Parliament voted last April to delay the municipal council and mayoral elections until April 1998 in a move that analysts said was largely due to fears among top political leaders that the results could undermine their power bases.

Parliament voted late on Wednesday for a further one-year delay after billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said he could not guarantee that a new local elections law would be ready for next spring.
The decision means Lebanon's municipal councils will 36 years old before they are finally renewed. The last local elections took place in 1963.
Most municipalities will be run by government appointees until the elections take place.
